transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello Dr. Smith. I have this intense, over-the-top fear of being up high in tall buildings that doesn’t match what I know is the actual risk, and it’s starting to interfere with my work.

Do you also experience significant fear or avoidance when you are in crowded places, public transportation, or other situations where you might feel trapped and unable to easily escape if you were to have a panic attack?

No, I don't experience any fear or avoidance with crowded places, public transit, or feeling trapped. My anxiety is strictly limited to heights and being up high in tall buildings. I don't have those other issues at all.
When you are exposed to heights, do you experience immediate physical symptoms like a racing heart, trembling, or a feeling of losing control?

Yes, definitely. As soon as I realize a meeting is on a high floor, my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel almost lightheaded. It actually starts happening just picturing the elevator ride and the view, even before I've stepped foot inside the building.
